Applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. in Case Crime No.662 of 2022 under Sections 363, 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station- Debai, District - Bulandshahr after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 18.01.2023 passed by Special Judge(POCSO Act)/Additional Sessions Judge, Bulandshahr.

sentences.text: Informant tried to search his daughter.
When she was not found, F.I.R. was lodged against applicant on 10.12.2022.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that there is a delay of six days in lodging F.I.R. which remained unexplained.

Victim was recovered on same day and her statement was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. that she was forcefully kidnapped by applicant who gave adulterated food item and after eating it she became unconscious and later on, when she became conscious, she found that her clothes were torn and applicant has committed rape on her.

Learned counsel further submits that though the victim's version remained same in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., however, she has not made any specific allegation of rape against applicant.
It was a case of love affair between victim and applicant and she on her own sweet will, had accompanied the applicant and lived along with him.

No Ossification test was conducted,
therefore, victim cannot be definitely considered to be a minor.
Applicant has no criminal history and he is in jail since 11.12.2022, therefore, he is entitled for bail.

Learned Brief Holder for State and learned counsel for informant have submitted that since minor daughter of informant was enticed away by applicant and in order to avoid social disgrace, initially informant was hesitating in lodging F.I.R. and as such delay of six days cannot be considered to be an adverse factor.

Victim has specifically stated that she was forcefully kidnapped by applicant who administered her with some sedative food and he raped her, even in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has not denied that she was not raped, but has stated that she had not clearly remembered what had happened, after she was put under sedation.
LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

sentences.text: In the present case, age of victim is about 13 years which cannot be doubted without any contrary material.
Victim remained consistent in her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. that applicant enticed her and kidnapped her from lawful guardianship.

She has specifically stated about act of rape in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., though, she has not specifically stated about act of rape in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., however, she has not denied either.
It was stated that she does not remember what happen after she was put under sedation.
The argument of learned counsel for applicant that it was a case of love affair, therefore, bail may be granted, cannot be accepted as in similar circumstances.

Supreme Court in case of X(Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Anr. in Criminal Appeal No. 263 of 2022 dated 21.02.2022 has dealt with situation as similar to present case and has considered the argument in regard to love-affair and relevant paragraph No.6 is reproduced hereinafter :-
"6.

entities.text: X(Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court was manifestly in error in allowing the application for bail.

The reason that from the statement under Section 164 and the averments in the FIR, it appears that "there was a love affair" between the appellant and the second respondent and that the case was instituted on the refusal of the second respondent to marry the appellant, is specious.

Once, prima facie, it appears from the material before the Court that the appellant was barely thirteen years of age on the date when the alleged offence took place, both the grounds, namely that "there was a love affair"
between the appellant and the second respondent as well as the alleged refusal to marry, are circumstances which will have no bearing on the grant of bail. Having regard to the age of the prosecutrix and the nature and gravity of the crime, no case for the grant of bail was established.

The order of the High Court granting bail has to be interfered with since the circumstances which prevailed with the High Court are extraneous in view of the age of the prosecutrix, having regard to the provisions of Section 376 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO."
In view of the above discussion of law and fact and materials and factors discussed above, applicant has failed to make out any case of bail.
Accordingly bail application is rejected.
